In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of legume-cereal intercropping systems is a good strategy for reducing the risk of crop failure, increasing the yield of the legume and the cereals and improving the economic viability of the crop production system.
winter pea and spring barley, winter pea and spring wheat, spring pea and winter rye, and spring pea and winter wheat are good associations for farmers to grow.

the use of legumes in cereal crops is a promising strategy to improve crop productivity, to reduce the use of nitrogen fertilizers and pesticides, to improve the quality of the cereal grain and to increase the profitability of the cropping system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
intercropping is a promising tool to increase stability and yield of grain legumes in Western Canada.
winter pea is a promising alternative for the farmers of the Western part of Belgium, especially in association with oats.
the association of cereals and legumes is beneficial for the cereals but not for the legumes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pea is a promising crop for organic farming in Quebec and that the association pea-barley is a promising option for the organic farmers of the West.
the pea-lupin association is a good option to reduce the risk of crop failures.
the use of legume crops is a viable alternative to reduce dependence on imported protein.
